brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.

requirements.requirement: A cabinet made of three cells (three hex base cells)
requirements.evidence: Three Hex base · Full pieces in a straight row at (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0), role R1 on the two outer ones; get_build lists 3 piece nodes, check_build clear, meshClash clear.

Two notch drawer frames, at (0,1) (female-male) and (0,-1) (male-female), each filling the gap between two touching bases. BOM lists 2 'Notch drawer' bodies plus their runners and lids. Note the configurator's find_sockets 'drawer' family returned nothing; the drawers are carried as notch frames with drawer bodies.

requirements.requirement: One of the two drawers is shown pulled open
requirements.evidence: setNotchOpen at (0,1), k=1, open=true returned ok. get_build does not expose the open state and I could not view it, so the open pose is confirmed only by the accepted op, not visually.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell cabinet: three full hex bases in a row, with two notch drawers in the two gaps (one above, one below the row). The north-side drawer at (0,1) is set open. Meshes clear and no rule errors. No props, covers or soil were added since the brief did not ask for them. Caveat: the open state is confirmed only by the accepted setNotchOpen op.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
